On 13 November 2024 the Supreme Court la: On 13 November 2024 the Supreme Court laid down binding directions: no demolition without a show-cause notice served by registered post and pasted on the structure, giving at least 15 days (or longer if local law allows) to reply; a personal hearing; a reasoned final order; a further 15 days before it is carried out so it can be challenged; and videography of any demolition. Officials who break these directions face contempt and must personally pay for restoration. The directions do not apply to unauthorised structures on public places such as roads, footpaths, railway lines or water bodies, or where a court has ordered demolition. Under the Street Vendors Act, 2014, no vendor may be evicted until the town’s vendor survey is complete and certificates issued (s.3(3)); eviction needs 30 days’ notice (s.18(3)); seized goods must be listed, and released the same day if perishable and within two working days otherwise (s.19). Slum eviction and rehabilitation depend on state law and policy; ask whether you were counted in the survey.

The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 gives ev: The Mental Healthcare Act, 2017 gives every person the right to access mental healthcare from government-funded services (s.18), to live with dignity and to be protected from cruel or degrading treatment (s.20), and to free legal services (s.27). Insurers must provide medical insurance for mental illness on the same basis as physical illness (s.21(4)). An adult may seek admission on their own (independent admission, s.86) and can ask to be discharged. Admission without the person’s consent (supported admission) needs specific conditions and lasts up to 30 days (s.89); longer stays need the Mental Health Review Board’s approval (s.90), and the Board hears appeals. Chaining, electroconvulsive therapy without anaesthesia and muscle relaxants, ECT for minors and sterilisation as treatment are banned (s.95). A person can make an advance directive and name a nominated representative. Private “rehab” or de-addiction centres must also follow the law.
